Settings.Quality.Help:
The preset sets the frame size, frame rate and picture quality. "Balanced" suits almost everyone: a sharp picture, small clips. "Maximum" records at the game's resolution and 60 frames per second, clips are noticeably heavier. "Custom" opens manual sliders.

If the game window is smaller than the chosen size, it is recorded as is, without stretching.

Capture. On Windows 10 the usual method draws a yellow border around the game: it does not appear in the recording, but you can see it. The "Borderless" mode removes it. If it fails with some game, the program falls back to standard capture by itself.

Changes take effect from the next launch of the game. During recording you can press "Apply now", and then whatever is stored in the buffer will be lost.
Settings.Buffer.Help:
The program keeps the last minutes of the game in memory at all times. Press the hotkey, and those minutes are saved as a clip. Nothing is written to disk until then.

Buffer length: how many of the last seconds go into the clip.
Quiet window: how long the program waits after a press. If you press again within that time, you get one longer clip instead of two.
Merge limit: the clip is not extended beyond this time after the first press, the next press starts a new one.

Below is how much memory the buffer will take with these settings.
Settings.Hotkey.Help:
The key combination that saves a clip. It works at all times, even while you are in a game and the program window is minimized. To change it, click it and press a new combination.

If the combination is already taken by another program, a warning appears here: choose a different one. For a single game you can set its own combination in its profile.
Settings.Games.Help:
Recording starts by itself when a game from the list launches, and stops when the game closes. Add a game with the "Add application" button or choose one from the running applications. The "Profile" button next to a game opens its own settings.

Automatic detection: if you launch something full screen that loads the graphics card, or a game from Steam, Epic or GOG, the program asks once whether to record it.

Record after the game exits: if the game closes or crashes, recording continues for a while with a black frame and sound, so the moment of the crash can be saved. If the game starts again in that time, recording continues without a break.

Switch to the game's larger window: for games that first show a small launcher and then the game's own window. Recording moves to the larger window, and the buffer accumulated before that is lost.
Settings.Sound.Help:
"Whole computer sound" records everything you hear: the game, music, voice chat. "Selected applications only" records only those, for example the game without the background music.

The microphone stays off until you turn it on. Noise suppression removes hum and fan noise from your voice.

Volume: 100 is the normal level of the source, above 100 amplifies it. The bars show the live level. If the overall sound is too loud, the program gently holds it back, and the "limiter" mark lights up.
Settings.Storage.Help:
Clips are saved here: one folder per game, and inside it one folder for each game session.

Limit folder size: when the clips take up more than the set amount, the oldest are deleted, if auto-delete is on. Clips with tags are never deleted.

Deleted clips go to the Windows recycle bin, so the space is freed only after it is emptied.
Settings.About.Help:
Version number and the project's GitHub address.

Check for updates: at startup and once a day the program asks GitHub for the latest version number. If a new one is out, a link to it appears in the window title. The program does not download anything itself. A dismissed line will not come back until the next version.
Settings.Profile.Help:
A profile changes settings for this game only. A group you have not touched takes its values from the common settings and follows them when they change.

The profile takes effect from the next launch of the game, the key combination changes immediately.
